title.narrative: Operation of the kidney dialysis center at Banadir Hospital in Mogadishu (phase three)

description.narrative: The project aims to establish an integrated hemodialysis center in Mogadishu, Banadir State. This specialized, free center is the only one of its kind in the region and is directly responsible for providing services to patients with kidney failure and other kidney diseases. In its current phase, the project targets serving 665 people monthly, including 195 registered dialysis patients receiving two to three dialysis sessions per week. This translates to approximately 1,500 dialysis sessions per month, totaling 18,000 sessions for the entire 12-month project duration. The center is equipped with 29 dialysis machines (25 new and 4 older) and a water treatment plant to supply them. Located within the main hospital in Banadir, the center can operate at a capacity of approximately 57 sessions per day, equivalent to 1,500 sessions per month. The center also includes a pharmacy providing medications for kidney failure patients and a specialized nephrology clinic, the only one of its kind in the region. Free in Mogadishu, the project includes a laboratory for conducting tests and provides employment for 59 staff members.

To meet the needs of kidney failure patients and ensure their access to necessary treatment free of charge, with an expected number of 18,000 dialysis sessions and 3,260 medical services at the nephrology clinic. The project also aims to support the resilience of the medical and technical staff and reduce the emigration of 59 medical and technical personnel, while localizing the service.

To provide healthcare services, specifically ensuring access to necessary treatment in Mogadishu, to preserve the lives of kidney patients and those suffering from renal failure due to lack of treatment, thereby reducing mortality rates through the provision of free treatment.
